title: feat: add editable prompt agents
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Depends on #13407 being deployed before Pollinations tools are enabled.

- Adds editable prompt agents with a system prompt, Pollinations base model, and public Streamable HTTP MCP servers.
- Runs every definition in one shared Enter Worker using Vercel AI SDK ToolLoopAgent and the official @ai-sdk/mcp client.
- Adds an opt-in Pollinations tools switch backed by `https://mcp.pollinations.ai`; external MCP servers never receive Pollinations credentials.
- Mints a short-lived ag_ token scoped to the caller parent key and managed agent, then uses it for base-model and built-in tool calls.
- Keeps agent definitions editable behind stable private/public My Models listings and requires managed-agent listings to remain free.
- Adds dashboard and polli agents CRUD without per-agent Workers, bundles, or persistent agent API keys.

V1 stays narrow: one agent per listing, no MCP OAuth/private headers, custom code, or versioning.

Validation: Enter and Gen typechecks, CLI build, 15 prompt-agent runtime tests, 7 run-token tests, and 6 focused managed-agent registration/delegation tests.

gist.headline: Agents, but editable
gist.blurb: The hive can now grow little prompt-powered helpers without growing a Worker farm behind them. Pick a model, write the instructions, plug in public MCP tools, and let the agent get to work.
gist.summary: Added editable prompt agents to My Models and the Polli CLI, letting users publish one-agent listings with a system prompt, a Pollinations base model, public Streamable HTTP MCP servers, and an opt-in set of Pollinations tools.
gist.impact: Developers can create, edit, list, and run managed agents without deploying per-agent Workers or maintaining persistent agent API keys, while short-lived ag_ tokens safely scope model and built-in tool access.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden workbench where Polli is tuning a small friendly prompt-agent seedling: a retro terminal shows editable instruction cards, a model selector, and branching tool-vines connecting to public MCP server signposts. A CRT monitor robot eagerly holds a tiny tool box while Polli, wearing mechanic goggles, adjusts the agent's settings; the scene communicates composable agents without a pile of separate servers.
